description: Comprehensive test strategy for the entire system based on complete architecture (SE-06-A05)

test_strategy_philosophy.purpose: Define testing strategy UPFRONT (in SE phase) so development implements tests per plan and operations executes tests
test_strategy_philosophy.principle: Testing is an ARCHITECTURAL decision, not an operational afterthought
test_strategy_philosophy.critical_note: Testing strategy defined HERE (SE phase), implemented in Development workflow (D-02 to D-05), executed in Testing workflow (TO-01 to TO-05). Testing phase does NOT invent new tests.
test_strategy_philosophy.risk_based: Focus effort on high-risk services (comprehensive testing) while avoiding over-testing low-risk services
test_strategy_philosophy.prevents: Toss-it-over-the-fence problem - developers know testing requirements upfront, operators execute pre-defined plan

applicability.applies_to: All frameworks (UAF, Biology, Social, Ecological, CAS, Custom)
applicability.note: Testing strategy is universal - all system types need validation, although specific test types may vary by framework

unit_test_strategy.description: Component-level testing strategy for individual services/components
unit_test_strategy.purpose: Validate individual components work correctly in isolation

coverage_targets.description: Minimum test coverage based on service risk level
coverage_targets.source: Risk levels from SE-02-A10 (risk_assessment.json per service)

high_risk_services.rationale: Critical services (payment, auth, data storage) require comprehensive testing

medium_risk_services.rationale: Important services require solid test coverage

low_risk_services.rationale: Non-critical services (logging, metrics) need basic coverage, not comprehensive

mocking_strategy.external_dependencies: Mock external systems (databases, message queues, third-party APIs)
mocking_strategy.internal_dependencies: Use real internal components where possible, mock only at service boundaries
mocking_strategy.rationale: Mocking external deps keeps tests fast and reliable; using real internal components catches integration issues early

test_organization.structure: Mirror source code structure in tests/ directory
test_organization.descriptive_names: Use descriptive test names: test_create_character_with_valid_data_returns_201() not test_create()
test_organization.arrange_act_assert: Follow AAA pattern: Arrange (setup), Act (execute), Assert (verify)

continuous_testing.frequency: Run on every commit via CI/CD pipeline
continuous_testing.failure_handling: Block pull request merge if tests fail or coverage drops below target
continuous_testing.fast_feedback: Unit tests should complete in < 5 minutes for rapid feedback

success_criteria: All services meet risk-based coverage targets (85% high-risk, 80% medium, 60% low)
All tests pass (zero failures)
Tests run in < 5 minutes
No flaky tests (tests that randomly fail)

integration_test_strategy.description: Cross-component testing strategy for service interactions
integration_test_strategy.purpose: Validate services work correctly together, catching interface mismatches and integration bugs

integration_targets.description: Which service pairs require integration tests
integration_targets.rule: Every edge in system graph requires at least one integration test

example_targets.edge_description: Create character → Use character in session
example_targets.test_scenario: Create character via character_service API, start session with character ID, verify session_service fetches character details
POST /login to api_gateway → api_gateway calls authentication_service → authentication_service validates credentials in user_service

test_environment.isolation: Each test suite gets fresh environment (or database transaction rollback)
test_environment.configuration: Use test-specific config (TEST_MODE=true, in-memory databases where applicable)

mocking_approach.external_systems: Mock third-party APIs (payment gateways, email services, external data sources)
mocking_approach.internal_services: Use real internal services (not mocks) to catch integration issues
mocking_approach.test_doubles: Use stubs for unavailable services during development, replace with real services before merge

data_setup_teardown.fixtures: Use test fixtures to create known data state before tests
data_setup_teardown.database_seeding: Seed test database with realistic data (users, entities, relationships)
data_setup_teardown.cleanup: Tear down data after each test (transaction rollback or DELETE operations)
data_setup_teardown.idempotency: Tests should be idempotent (can run multiple times without side effects)

contract_tests.description: Consumer-driven contract tests ensure API compatibility
contract_tests.approach: Consumer defines expected contract, provider validates implementation matches
contract_tests.example: character_service (consumer) defines contract for session_service API (provider), session_service validates it provides expected responses

success_criteria: All service pairs (edges in system graph) have at least one integration test
Integration tests pass in test environment (Docker Compose)
Tests catch interface mismatches (wrong response format, missing fields)
Tests complete in < 10 minutes

contract_test_strategy.description: Consumer-driven contract testing for all external-facing APIs
contract_test_strategy.purpose: Prevent breaking changes to APIs that would break consumers

workflow: 1. Consumer defines expected contract (request format, response format, status codes)
2. Contract published to contract repository (Git repo or Pact Broker)
3. Provider fetches contract and validates implementation matches
4. Provider runs contract tests on every commit (CI/CD)
approach.benefit: Consumers specify what they need, providers guarantee compatibility - prevents 'it works on my machine' integration failures

pact.name: Pact
pact.features: Consumer-driven contracts, Pact Broker for contract sharing, CI/CD integration
pact.example: Consumer: pact-python library; Provider: pytest-pact plugin

spring_cloud_contract.name: Spring Cloud Contract
spring_cloud_contract.features: Contract-first API development, stub generation, consumer/provider testing

verify_component_contract.name: verify_component_contract.py
verify_component_contract.use_case: Validate service implementation matches service_architecture.json contract

contract_targets.rule: All interfaces with external_api: true in interface_registry.json require contract tests

contract_includes: POST /characters with invalid data returns 400 + error details

versioning_strategy.major_version: Breaking changes (field removed, field type changed, required field added) → Increment major version (v1 → v2)
versioning_strategy.minor_version: Backward-compatible additions (new optional field, new endpoint) → Increment minor version (v2.1 → v2.2)
versioning_strategy.patch_version: Bug fixes (no API changes) → Increment patch version (v2.1.1 → v2.1.2)
versioning_strategy.compatibility: Providers must support current major version + previous major version for 6 months (e.g., v2.x and v1.x simultaneously)

provider_validation_frequency.frequency: On every commit to provider service (CI/CD pipeline)
provider_validation_frequency.failure_handling: Block merge if contract tests fail (provider broke contract with consumer)
provider_validation_frequency.notification: Notify consumers when provider makes breaking changes (even if major version bump planned)

success_criteria: All external APIs have contract tests (coverage = 100% of external_api interfaces)
Contract tests run on every provider commit
Breaking changes detected before merge
Versioning strategy enforced (breaking change = major version bump)

performance_test_strategy.description: Load, stress, and endurance testing to validate system performance
performance_test_strategy.purpose: Ensure system handles expected traffic and degrades gracefully under stress

test_types.purpose: Verify system handles expected traffic without degradation

scenarios.description: Normal production traffic
Traffic spike (e.g., marketing campaign)
Severe traffic spike

test_types.purpose: Find breaking point and verify graceful degradation

scenarios.description: Increase load incrementally until system fails
steps: Continue until error rate > 5% or latency > 5 seconds
scenarios.metrics: Record breaking point (max throughput before failure)

scenarios.description: Verify system recovers when load decreases
steps: Verify system recovers (latency returns to baseline, error rate drops to 0%)

success_criteria.graceful_degradation: System returns 503 Service Unavailable (not crashes) when overloaded
success_criteria.no_data_corruption: Database integrity maintained even during overload
success_criteria.automatic_recovery: System recovers when load decreases (no manual intervention)

test_types.purpose: Verify stability over time (detect memory leaks, resource exhaustion)

scenarios.description: Run at expected load continuously for 24 hours
metrics: Memory usage (should be stable, not growing)

scenarios.description: Extended soak test for critical services

success_criteria.no_memory_leaks: Memory usage stable (< 5% growth over 24 hours)
success_criteria.no_resource_exhaustion: No disk full, no connection pool exhaustion, no file descriptor limits hit

availability.downtime_allowed: 8.76 hours per year (43.8 minutes per month)
availability.measurement: Percentage of successful requests over time window

latency.rationale: p95 is more important than average - represents typical user experience

throughput.calculation: Based on expected user count and usage patterns
throughput.example: 10,000 concurrent users × 1 request per 10 seconds = 1,000 req/sec

error_rate.target: < 0.1% under normal load (1 error per 1000 requests)

risk_based_performance_testing.high_risk_services: Load at 5x traffic, stress testing, 48-hour soak tests
risk_based_performance_testing.medium_risk_services: Load at 2x traffic, stress testing, 24-hour soak test (optional)

success_criteria: All services meet latency targets (p95 < 500ms at 2x load)
High-risk services tested at 5x load and pass
Soak tests show no memory leaks or resource exhaustion
System degrades gracefully under stress (returns 503, not crashes)

security_test_strategy.description: Vulnerability and penetration testing to ensure system security
security_test_strategy.purpose: Identify and remediate security vulnerabilities before production

test_types.description: Test for common web application vulnerabilities

vulnerabilities.name: Injection
vulnerabilities.test: SQL injection, NoSQL injection, command injection, LDAP injection

vulnerabilities.name: Insecure Design
vulnerabilities.test: Missing security controls, threat modeling gaps

vulnerabilities.name: Security Misconfiguration
vulnerabilities.test: Default credentials, unnecessary features enabled, verbose errors

vulnerabilities.name: Authentication Failures
vulnerabilities.test: Weak passwords, session fixation, credential stuffing

test_types.frequency: Before each production release + quarterly thereafter
test_types.success_criteria: Zero high/critical vulnerabilities, all medium vulnerabilities have mitigation plans

test_types.description: Scan third-party libraries for known vulnerabilities (CVEs)
test_types.scope: All third-party dependencies (npm packages, pip packages, Maven dependencies)
test_types.failure_handling: Block merge if critical vulnerabilities detected
test_types.remediation: Update dependencies to patched versions, or document mitigation if update not possible
test_types.success_criteria: No critical vulnerabilities, all high vulnerabilities patched or mitigated within 7 days

test_types.scope: All Docker images used in production
test_types.success_criteria: No critical vulnerabilities in production images
test_types.remediation: Use minimal base images (alpine, distroless), keep base images updated

test_types.description: Manual security assessment by security professionals
test_types.performed_by: External security firm (preferred) or internal red team
methodology: Black-box testing (no source code access, simulates external attacker)
White-box testing (full source code access, comprehensive review)
Gray-box testing (partial knowledge, simulates insider threat)
test_types.deliverable: Penetration test report with findings categorized by severity, remediation recommendations, and target dates
test_types.success_criteria: No critical findings, all high findings remediated before production

test_types.description: Automated source code analysis for security vulnerabilities
test_types.success_criteria: Zero critical issues, high issues reviewed and fixed or false-positive confirmed

test_types.approach: Crawl application, identify attack surface, attempt exploits

risk_based_security_testing.high_risk_services: Full suite (OWASP, dependency scan, container scan, pentesting, SAST, DAST)
risk_based_security_testing.medium_risk_services: Standard suite (OWASP, dependency scan, container scan, SAST)

success_criteria: All security tests pass (or findings remediated)
Zero critical vulnerabilities in production
All medium/high vulnerabilities have documented mitigation plans with target dates
Penetration test report shows no exploitable critical vulnerabilities

operational_test_strategy.description: Operational acceptance testing - validates system survives real operational conditions
operational_test_strategy.purpose: Prevent 'toss it over the fence' problem - validate deployment readiness BEFORE operational testing
operational_test_strategy.note: This is the FOCUS of Reflow v3.6.0 Early Testing Integration feature

pre_operational_validation.purpose: Catch 80-90% of deployment blockers BEFORE operational testing
validation_categories: Module structure (no circular imports, no missing __init__.py)
Database permissions (migrations run as service user)
Docker build validation (all services build successfully)
pre_operational_validation.blocking: MUST pass all D-06.5 checks before operational testing begins

scenarios.description: Deploy system from scratch (empty database, no existing state)
steps: 1. Start fresh environment (docker-compose down -v to remove volumes)
3. Wait for all services to report healthy (/health returns 200)
scenarios.success_criteria: All services start healthy within 2 minutes, smoke tests pass, no ERROR logs

scenarios.description: Deploy new version over existing system (schema migration, existing data)
steps: 1. Start with previous version running and data in database
2. Deploy new version: docker-compose pull && docker-compose up -d
scenarios.success_criteria: Migrations complete successfully, services restart healthy, existing data not corrupted, smoke tests pass

scenarios.description: Revert to previous version if deployment fails
steps: 1. Deploy new version that fails (simulate failure)
2. Detect failure (health checks fail, smoke tests fail)
3. Execute rollback: docker-compose down && git checkout <previous-tag> && docker-compose up -d
4. Verify system returns to healthy state
scenarios.success_criteria: Rollback completes in < 5 minutes, system returns to healthy state, no data loss

test_types.success_criteria: All deployment scenarios pass, no manual intervention required

test_types.purpose: Validate high availability and automatic recovery

scenarios.description: Primary database fails, system fails over to standby replica
steps: 4. System switches to standby replica (automatic or manual trigger)
5. Verify services recover and continue operating
scenarios.success_criteria: Failover completes within RTO (Recovery Time Objective, e.g., 30 seconds), no data loss within RPO (Recovery Point Objective, e.g., 5 minutes)

scenarios.description: Service instance crashes, orchestrator restarts it
steps: 1. System running with 3 instances of service
scenarios.success_criteria: Instance restarted within 30 seconds, no user-visible errors (load balancer routes to healthy instances)

scenarios.description: Network split causes services to lose connectivity (split-brain scenario)
steps: 2. Simulate network partition (iptables rules blocking traffic between AZs)
3. Observe split-brain handling (does system elect new leader? does it halt writes?)
scenarios.success_criteria: No data corruption, system handles split-brain correctly (e.g., uses quorum to prevent divergence), automatic reconciliation when network restored

scenarios.description: Entire availability zone fails
steps: 1. System running across 3 AZs (e.g., us-east-1a, us-east-1b, us-east-1c)
2. Simulate AZ failure (all instances in us-east-1a down)
3. Traffic automatically routed to remaining AZs
5. When AZ recovers, instances rejoin cluster
scenarios.success_criteria: System continues operating (degraded mode acceptable), no user data loss, automatic recovery when AZ returns

test_types.success_criteria: All failover scenarios complete within RTO, no data loss within RPO, automatic recovery (no manual intervention)

test_types.purpose: Inject failures to validate resilience and graceful degradation
test_types.applicability: Required ONLY for high-risk services (score >= 2.6 from SE-02-A10)
test_types.rationale: Chaos testing is expensive and time-consuming - focus on high-risk services only

scenarios.description: Randomly kill service instances (Chaos Monkey pattern)
scenarios.frequency: Kill 1 random instance every 5 minutes for 30 minutes
scenarios.expected_behavior: System continues operating, orchestrator restarts killed instances, no user-visible errors

scenarios.description: Add artificial network latency between services
scenarios.latency: Add 500ms or 1000ms latency to service-to-service calls
scenarios.expected_behavior: Timeouts trigger circuit breakers, fallback mechanisms activate, system returns degraded responses (not errors)

scenarios.description: Stress individual services with high CPU or memory usage
scenarios.stress: Consume 100% CPU for 5 minutes, or fill memory to limit
scenarios.expected_behavior: Orchestrator kills overloaded instance (OOMKilled), restarts it, system recovers automatically

scenarios.description: Fill disk to capacity
scenarios.expected_behavior: Service detects disk full, stops accepting writes, logs error, returns 503 (not crashes), recovers when disk space freed

scenarios.description: Kill downstream dependency to test circuit breaker and fallback
steps: 1. Service A depends on Service B
3. Service A detects B is down (health check fails or requests timeout)
4. Circuit breaker trips in Service A
5. Service A returns fallback response (cached data, default value, or 503)
7. Circuit breaker closes (requests to B succeed)
scenarios.expected_behavior: Circuit breaker trips, no cascading failure, fallback mechanism works, automatic recovery

success_criteria: System continues operating under chaos (degraded mode acceptable)
No cascading failures (one failure doesn't bring down entire system)
Automatic recovery when chaos stops
Circuit breakers trip and recover correctly
Fallback mechanisms provide degraded responses (not errors)

scenarios.description: Verify automated backup runs successfully
steps: 1. Trigger scheduled backup (e.g., pg_dump for PostgreSQL)
3. Verify backup file size reasonable (not empty, not suspiciously small)
4. Verify backup stored in backup location (S3, backup server)
scenarios.success_criteria: Backup completes within expected time, backup file valid

scenarios.description: Restore database to specific timestamp
steps: 1. Note current timestamp and database state
2. Make changes to database (insert, update, delete)
3. Trigger point-in-time restore to timestamp before changes
4. Verify database state matches expected state at that timestamp
scenarios.success_criteria: Restore completes within RTO, data matches expected state, integrity validated (checksums match)

scenarios.description: Complete system restore from backup (simulates catastrophic failure)
steps: 1. Destroy all system state (docker-compose down -v, delete databases)
scenarios.success_criteria: System fully operational after restore, data integrity validated, restore completes within RTO (e.g., 2 hours)

test_types.success_criteria: Backups complete successfully, restores work correctly, system functional after restore, data integrity maintained

operational_acceptance_criteria.description: System ready for production when these criteria met

criteria.validation: All 7 D-06.5 validation checks pass (dependencies, module structure, config, DB permissions, Docker build, smoke tests, contracts)
Cold start, upgrade, and rollback scenarios complete successfully
Database failover, service instance failure, network partition, multi-AZ failover all recover within RTO
criteria.applicability: Required only if HA is architectural requirement

criteria.validation: System survives random failures, degrades gracefully, recovers automatically
Backups complete successfully, restore tested and verified

success_criteria: D-06.5 pre-deployment validation passes (BLOCKING)
All deployment scenarios pass (cold start, upgrade, rollback)
Failover tests pass (if HA required)
Chaos tests pass (if high-risk services present)
Backup/restore validated

risk_based_testing_matrix.description: Testing requirements based on service risk level (from SE-02-A10 risk_assessment.json)

testing_requirements.performance_tests: Load at 5x traffic, stress testing, 48-hour soak test
testing_requirements.security_tests: Full suite (OWASP, dependency scan, container scan, pentesting, SAST, DAST)
testing_requirements.operational_tests: Deployment tests, failover tests, chaos tests (REQUIRED), backup/restore

high_risk_services.rationale: High-risk services (payment, auth, data storage) justify comprehensive testing - failures have severe impact

testing_requirements.performance_tests: Load at 2x traffic, stress testing, 24-hour soak test (optional)
testing_requirements.security_tests: Standard suite (OWASP, dependency scan, container scan, SAST)

medium_risk_services.rationale: Important services require solid testing but not comprehensive (focus effort on high-risk)

low_risk_services.rationale: Low-risk services (logging, metrics) don't justify comprehensive testing - avoid over-testing

development_workflow.d_06_5_validation: D-06.5 pre-deployment validation runs before operational testing

testing_workflow.responsibility: Executes operational tests per this strategy (deployment, failover, chaos, backup/restore)

All risk_assessment.json files (risk levels → testing thoroughness)
llm_agent_guidance.risk_based_testing: High-risk services (>= 2.6) MUST have chaos, load (5x), failover, pentesting. Medium-risk (1.6-2.5) get load (2x) + contract tests. Low-risk (< 1.6) get basic tests only.
llm_agent_guidance.integration_targets: EVERY edge in system_of_systems_graph.json requires at least one integration test - iterate through edges, create test scenarios
llm_agent_guidance.contract_targets: EVERY interface with external_api: true in interface_registry.json requires contract test
llm_agent_guidance.operational_testing_focus: D-06.5 pre-deployment validation catches 80-90% of blockers BEFORE operational testing - reference D-06.5 in operational test strategy
llm_agent_guidance.handoff_clarity: Make it clear: Testing strategy defined HERE, implemented in Development (D-02 to D-05), executed in Testing (TO-01 to TO-05). Testing phase does NOT invent tests.
llm_agent_guidance.avoid_over_testing: Don't require comprehensive testing for low-risk services - it wastes effort. Focus on high-risk (payment, auth, data storage).
llm_agent_guidance.critical_note: This strategy prevents 'toss it over the fence' problem - developers know testing requirements upfront, operators execute pre-defined plan.
